dedupe_keys.name: regional county level housing inventory predictions and the effects on hurricane risk using long short term memory lstm methods and applied to the southeastern united states us

description: Regional county-level housing inventory predictions and the effects on hurricane risk using long-short term memory (LSTM) methods and applied to the southeastern United States (US) is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "simulation", published or maintained by Rachel Davidson, University of Delaware (udel.edu). This project provides estimates of the projected annual number of housing units for each of 1,000 counties in coastal states from Delaware to Texas over a 10-, 20-, and 30-year time horizon (2020-2029, 2020-2039, 2020-2049, respectively), using a long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network model. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "simulation" project. Keywords: hurricane, housing inventory, machine learning, built environment, exposure, regional. Published 2022-02-17. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
